Thanks for the diagram, Sophie — good context. Following up from today's kickoff with the technical items we agreed on and the minimal config your infra team will need to prepare. I kept the notes terse to make it actionable.

Technical checklist (action items for Bridgeway IT):
1) VPC peering
   - Peer Redwood run-time VPC (rw-runtime-us-east-1) with Bridgeway app VPC (account: 843210987654)
   - Export/import route tables: announce 10.40.0.0/16 from Bridgeway; accept 10.128.0.0/16 from Redwood
   - Set TTL and route propagation per your infra standards; no transitive peering required

2) Private endpoints & DNS
   - We'll provision interface endpoints in us-east-1; please provide internal DNS zone name and whether you prefer split-horizon DNS
   - For certs: internal CA acceptance is fine; we will support mTLS for control plane calls to the appliance

3) On-prem appliance (colo)
   - NICs: 2x 1G (mgmt + data); recommend 1x 10G if you expect burst ingress >500 Mbps
   - Outbound: allow tcp 443 to Redwood control plane IPs (will provide CIDR) and tcp 123 for NTP if you block outbound
   - Syslog: optional — if you want logs forwarded to your SIEM, provide an endpoint and port

4) Firewall & NAT
   - Avoid source NAT for internal IPs across peering; keep traffic 10.x preserved so logs match

5) Audit/retention
   - Appliance supports local 90-day logs + remote syslog. If you need longer retention we can enable S3 export to your account (pricing note in MAP).

Next steps and owners:
- Bridgeway to confirm VPC account number and internal DNS zone (Raj) — due: 2026-12-10
- Redwood infra will produce a concise runbook and list of control-plane CIDRs (Irene) — due: 2026-12-08
- On-prem manifest finalized (Mateo + Monica) and shared with colo ops — due: 2026-12-12

Attachment: onprem-install-manifest.xlsx (updated during call)
